Robot Control Basics — Entry Point

Robot technicians, integrators and the operators who teach and supervise a cell; no union apprenticeship

ISO 10218 for the safety of industrial robots, ANSI/RIA R15.06 for their adoption in North America, and the teach-pendant and e-stop rules a cell is commissioned against

The entry point for controlling a robot safely: jog it from the pendant at a safe speed, measure what a cobot may touch, set up speed and separation monitoring, and bring it back after an e-stop. The stations are the robot-control ones and the stop rule they all share; the ROS-specific stations are not written yet, and this pack says so rather than claim them.

The ladder

What it proves

Competency: Robot Control Basics — Entry Point

No programme competency is registered for this track.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: ISO 10218 for the safety of industrial robots, ANSI/RIA R15.06 for their adoption in North America, and the teach-pendant and e-stop rules a cell is commissioned against. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
